AIRCRAFT — ELECTRICAL CABLES — 
IDENTIFICATION MARKING 



UDC 629-73-621-315-21 : 621 — 777

MANAK BHAVAN, 9 BAHADUR SHAH ZAFAR MARO 
NEW DELHI 110002

Aircraft Electrical Equipments Sectional Committee, TED 15 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Aircraft Electrical Equipments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Transport 
Engineering Division Council. 

In order to achieve international coordination on the subject this standard is based on ISO 2574 : 
1974 'Aircraft-electrical cables — Identification marking' issued by the International Organization 
for Standardization ( ISO ). 

The Committee composition responsible for the preparation of this standard is given at Annex A. 



IS 13932 : 1994 



Indian Standard 



AIRCRAFT — ELECTRICAL CABLES 
IDENTIFICATION MARKING 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard specifies the way in which 
single-core cables ( wires ) used in the wiring of 
aircraft are to be marked as to type, size, 
origin, date, etc, in order to facilitate servicing, 
the investigation of faults and replacement, 
when necessary, with an equivalent cables. 

1.2 It allows for manufacturer's own certifica- 
tion for easy identification of their cables. 

2 CABLE IDENTIFICATION 

2.1 Because of variation in requirements for 
cable coverings, the minimum size of cables that 
can be marked shall depend upon the overall 
diameter and shall be stated in the individual 
cable specification. 



2.2 The marking shall consist of a legend 
printed in a contrasting colour to that of the 
covering, of the size and of the characters 
required by the standard, repeated at intervals 
of 150 to 500 mm, and containing the following 
information: 

a) Name of cable ( wire ) or number of 
specification, type and size; 

b) Source of manufacture; and 

c) Year of manufacture. 

Dashes shall be used to separate name or 
specification, type, size and letter code detailed 
above, for example: 



( Specification ) — ( Type ) 
( Manufacturer ) — ( Year ) 



( Size ) — 



18 13932:1994

Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to 
promote harmonious development of the activities of stadardization, marking and quality 
certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced 
in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, 
in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type 
or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director 
( Publications ), BIS. 

Revision of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards 
are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review 
indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken 
up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the 
latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 'BIS Handbook* and 'Standards 
Monthly Additions*. 

This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc : No. TED 15 ( 047 )»
